newsitem.title: INDIA: INDIA CONGRESS SAYS WAITING FOR OIL PRICE MOVE.
newsitem.headline: INDIA CONGRESS SAYS WAITING FOR OIL PRICE MOVE.

text.p: India's Congress party said on Wednesday that it would not give its views on a proposed hike in petroleum prices until the ruling centre-left coalition comes out with a formal proposal.
"First of all there must be a formal proposal from the government," Pranab Mukherjee, former finance minister and a leading Congress economic ideologue, told Reuters.
Mukherjee was responding to a question on a report in Business Standard newspaper that his party was opposed to a fuel price hike planned by Prime Minister Inder Kumar Gujral's United Front.

The Front's decision-making Steering Committee was scheduled to meet at 5 p.m. (1130 GMT) to consider hikes in the prices of diesel and liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) to lower a deficit placed at 155 billion rupees ($4.34 billion) on March 31.
Mukherjee said Congress leaders had asked Gujral during a meeting to come out with a comprehensive plan to reduce the deficit.
Last week the Congress, which lends make-or-break support to the United Front, said the deficit was threatening India's fiscal stability.
"We said it is not that a mere ad-hoc increase will solve the problem," Mukherjee said.
Mukherjee said differences within the coalition were more important in dealing with the deficit.
"It is for them (United Front) to settle the issue," he said. "Thereafter we can give our view."
"The government of the day has to take a view and decide. How could we help if there are differences within the constituents of the government?," Mukherjee said.
Communist parties have led opposition within the United Front to any hike in the price of diesel or kerosene, which they say could stoke inflation or hurt the poor. ($1=35.7 rupees)
